extraction.teacher_style: The teachers provide clear, step-by-step instructions with a focus on body mechanics and weight distribution. They use a combination of verbal cues and visual demonstrations to ensure the student understands each movement.

lesson_structure.note: The teachers introduce the Pachanga basic step.
The teachers explain the bounce and the knee movement.
The teachers explain the leg movement.
The teachers explain the turn on the heels.
The teachers explain the weight change and the toe movement.
The teachers demonstrate the Salsa basic and the transition to the Pachanga basic.
The teachers add upper body movement to the basic step.
The teachers practice the steps with music.

metaphors: kicking this leg to the front
common_mistakes: turning on the toes instead of the heels
putting the leg too far behind
safety: keep the angle between your hip and your upper body

steps_taught.name: Pachanga basic
steps_taught.description: A dance step involving a bounce, leg movement, and a turn on the heels.

what_works: The teachers break down the steps into small, manageable parts.
They provide clear verbal and visual cues.
what_hinders: The teachers do not provide a slow-motion demonstration of the full step.

quotes.text: The most important part for Pachanga is the bounce.
Which would be wrong is when we bend also this ankle.
Try not to put the leg too far behind.
Many people they start to turn on the toes instead of the heels.
It's a bit like we're kicking this leg to the front.
It's a small movement, but it's going to add at the end for a more flowy look.
